item.text: I’m using a warm cream-and-olive palette, a large pancake photo, and an editorial layout. The page will also include ingredient checkboxes, a saved-recipe button, and a print view.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > index.html <<'EOF' <"'!DOCTYPE html> Lemon Ricotta Pancakes · Sunday Table
Sunday Table.
RecipesKitchen notesAboutGood food. Slow moments.
HomeBreakfast & brunchLemon ricotta pancakes
A brighter kind of breakfast

Lemon ricotta
pancakes

Golden edges, pillowy middles, and a little lemon sunshine. These are the pancakes that turn an ordinary morning into a slow Sunday.

TOTAL TIME
25 minutes
SERVINGS
4 people
DIFFICULTY
Easy does it
Jump to recipe
SFrom the Sunday kitchenMade with a little love
BRIGHT & FLUFFYA SUNDAY FAVORITE

A little zest. A lot of joy.

LET’S MAKE SOMETHING GOOD

Your new morning ritual.

Ingredients

Serves 4

A few simple things, something wonderful.

Let’s get cooking

25 minutes, start to finish

  1. Start with the good stuff

    In a large bowl, whisk together the ricotta, milk, eggs, and lemon zest until well combined. A few little ricotta curds are perfectly lovely.

  2. Keep it light

    Add the flour, sugar, baking powder, and a pinch of salt. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until just combined. Don’t overmix.

  3. A little pause

    Let the batter rest for 5 minutes. Just enough time to put the kettle on and warm up your pan.

  4. Golden, then flip

    Heat a little butter in a pan over medium heat. Spoon in the batter and cook until bubbles form on the surface. Flip once, then cook the other side until golden and cooked through.

A note from the kitchen

Gentle folding is the secret to fluffy pancakes. Serve them warm, straight from the pan. A drizzle of maple syrup and a little extra lemon zest make a lovely finishing touch.

Here’s to taking mornings a little slower.
Sunday Table.

Simple recipes. Seasonal inspiration. A seat for everyone.

Made for the everyday, and the just-because.
EOF python3 - <<'PY' from pathlib import Path import base64 p = Path('index.html') s = p.read_text() s = s.replace('__PANCAKE_IMAGE__', 'data:image/jpeg;base64,' + base64.b64encode(Path('/tmp/pancakes-warm.jpg').read_bytes()).decode()) s = s.replace('', '') p.write_text(s) PY"
